text.title: django-coding-standards Core Rules
text.summary: Nine testable rules for Django repo layout and code conventions.

rule.statement: Repository tree: `apps/<app>/` for domain apps, `core/` for cross-cutting code (BaseModel, mixins, permissions), `config/` for settings (`base.py`, `development.py`, `production.py`, `test.py`). No code at the repo root.
rule.rationale: Predictable layout enables agents and humans to navigate without grep. Repo-root code resists testing and breaks `python -m` invocations.

rule.statement: Cross-app imports MUST be aliased: `from apps.users.models import User as users_models_User`. Direct symbol imports (`from apps.users.models import User`) are forbidden — they clash on common names (User, Status).
rule.rationale: Multiple apps inevitably define `User` or `Status`. Aliasing prevents shadowing and makes the source app explicit at the import site.

rule.statement: Business logic lives in `apps/<app>/services/<topic>.py`. Views call services. Services orchestrate models, utils, and integrations. Tasks are thin wrappers over services. Utils are pure functions.
rule.rationale: Layering keeps each layer testable in isolation. Logic in views / utils / models defeats testability and concentrates churn in the wrong layer.

rule.statement: Service functions declare keyword-only arguments after `*`. `def create_user(*, email: str, name: str, role: Role) -> User:`.
rule.rationale: Positional args produce silent bugs on signature change (swap two args of the same type). Keyword-only forces every callsite to be explicit.

rule.statement: Use `models.TextChoices` (or `IntegerChoices`) for enums. Centralise in `apps/<app>/constants.py`. Never use plain strings for status / kind / role.
rule.rationale: TextChoices give a typed enum, a `.choices` form for Django forms, and a translation-ready label. Plain strings drift and produce typos that bypass validation.

rule.statement: Every `instance.save(update_fields=[...])` lists the changed fields. Bare `instance.save()` is allowed only on creation.
rule.rationale: Bare save() writes all fields; signals fire for unrelated changes; auditing produces noise. `update_fields` makes the write surface explicit and avoids contention.

rule.statement: When the project is Django 5.x or 4.2 LTS on Python 3.12+, the code lives under `apps/<app>/` or `core/`, `pytest + pytest-django` is configured and service-layer separation is agreed, the standards audit MUST run on a named trigger - a new app added under `apps/`, or the Django version pin in `pyproject.toml` changing - and MUST produce the 02-output-contract record with all six fields computed from the tree: `layout` read from the directory structure, `cross_app_imports_aliased` from `templates/django_import_lint.py`, `update_fields_on_save` from a scan for bare `.save()` outside creation paths, and the service-layer, keyword-only and TextChoices flags from the source, never from a self-assessment.

rationale.source: Two Scoops of Django; Django docs - Model.save() update_fields

rule.rationale: Five of the six fields are `const: true`, so a record filled in by hand is always valid and never wrong. Computing each flag from the tree and the lint is the only way fm-02 (shadowed `User` import) and fm-06 (bare save) show up as a red field instead of a production bug.

rule.statement: When the preconditions hold but a required field cannot be computed - `pyproject.toml` carries no Django version pin, `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` is absent so the lint and tests cannot run, or `layout` would be `mixed` because code still sits under `myproject/` or the repo root with Step 1 of the procedure unfinished - the audit MUST block naming the missing prerequisite from the Prerequisites table, and MUST NOT emit a record asserting the five `const: true` flags over a partial tree.

rationale.source: pytest-django docs - Configuring Django settings; Two Scoops of Django

rule.rationale: A record with `layout: mixed` and all flags true is schema-valid and reads as a passed audit while half the code was never scanned. Blocking on the named prerequisite makes the incomplete migration visible to the owner instead of hiding it behind a green record.

rule.statement: When any Applies-If fails or any Skip-If holds - the project is not Django (FastAPI, Flask), it is a throwaway tool with no growth horizon, or the `apps/core/config` layout is not adopted and refactoring it is out of scope - the methodology MUST NOT be applied; the skip MUST be recorded against the evidence anchor (the `pyproject.toml` commit or the ticket) naming the failed precondition and the route taken instead (the framework-specific methodology for non-Django; `django-models`, `django-pytest` or `django-api` when only one area is in scope), and a `layout: flat` record MUST NOT be filed as a completed audit.
rule.rationale: A flat throwaway tool and a flat production codebase that refused the refactor produce the same `layout: flat` record; only the anchored skip says which one it was and when the question reopens. Without it the refactor that was deferred for one quarter is deferred forever.
